title: My Own Application
encoding: WebP quality94 from generated PNG, without resize or composition changes
sourceCredit: Anh Vu Sawyer · The Moth Radio Hour, “Live and Learn”
imagePrompt: Create one landscape 1536 x 1024 production sprite atlas: exactly TWO columns and THREE rows, six wide cinematic full-scene panels in row-major order 0,1 / 2,3 / 4,5. Each cell fills approximately 768 x 341 pixels (last row 342), flush edge to edge, no gutters or borders. Every cell is a standalone wide composition, not a square image pasted on a wide matte. Painterly literary motion-comic art: watercolor pigment, restrained ink contours, colored-pencil texture, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, grounded feet, credible hands, soft practical light. Keep faces and essential hand/object contact comfortably inside the cell. Show seated bodies joined naturally to chair and table; include chair seats, knees, ankles and shoes when visible. No detached limbs, paper-doll joints, rigid mannequin poses, extra fingers or floating props. Keep cast, clothing, anatomy, furniture and setting consistent across relevant cells. These are fictional adaptation illustrations, not portraits or photographs of real source subjects. NO lettering, labels, logos, readable writing, panel numbers, captions, speech text or watermarks anywhere. Chapter: My Own Application. Cast/design continuity: A fictional 64-year-old woman mentor with softly lined face, short silver-streaked dark hair, round glasses, slate cardigan and comfortable skirt; a young male student with curly dark hair and mustard sweater. Quiet school courtyard, stone bench, open college gates in the distance. Blank paper application is a real object.. CELL 0: Wide school courtyard. The mentor stands naturally beside the student, her weight on one foot, one open hand directing him toward distant college gates. A folded application corner protrudes from her cardigan pocket. Warm morning light, modest purposeful gesture. CELL 1: Same courtyard and people. The student bends slightly to pick up the escaped folded paper, then offers it at a believable hand height. The mentor turns toward him with mild surprise; neither stares at viewer. Both hands and the paper remain clearly connected. CELL 2: Both seated on the stone bench. The mentor looks down and smooths the worn fold of the application across her lap while the student sits beside her listening. Her shoulders soften; the gates remain distant, not triumphantly glowing. CELL 3: Same bench, shifted natural posture. The student leans slightly toward her and gently indicates the gate with an open palm, returning her advice without lecturing. She looks between his face and the application, considering rather than smiling instantly. CELL 4: The mentor at a small courtyard writing table, fully seated and grounded. One hand steadies the unfolded application and the other holds a pencil touching its blank signature area. Her face shows deliberate concentration; student stands quietly a pace behind. No readable marks. CELL 5: Wide courtyard departure. The mentor walks slowly toward the open college gate with the folded application held securely in one hand. Student remains near the bench, pleased but unobtrusive. Her silver hair, glasses and clothing remain unchanged; no makeover or graduation fantasy.
